title: Commit Generator - public implementations survey
definition: Groups changes into documented version-control commits.
description:
Commit Generator is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Groups changes into documented version-control commits. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Commit Generator. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Commit Generator. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Commit Generator capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

title: Mercurial - related Commit Generator technology
definition: Clean distributed VCS alternative.
description:
Mercurial is not itself a Commit Generator, but it belongs in this survey because real Commit Generator work leans on it. Clean distributed VCS alternative.

In a Commit Generator build it shows up when startup speed beats raw peak power. The design favors boring reliability over cleverness: well-trodden paths, clear errors, and behavior you can reason about without reading the source. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best Commit Generator practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, Mercurial is a strong default choice as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Commit Generator
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Commit Generator

description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Commit Generator from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Commit Generator needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.
